subject: Ludwig van Beethoven
overview: Ludwig van Beethoven was a composer and pianist from Bonn who made his career in Vienna, where he earned an early reputation as a pianist and improviser. As his hearing deteriorated, he kept composing, writing piano sonatas, string quartets and symphonies that stretched the musical forms he had inherited.

key_moments.title: From Bonn to Vienna
key_moments.text: Beethoven moved from Bonn to Vienna, where he studied composition with **Joseph Haydn**. He gained an early reputation there for playing and improvising at the piano.
claims: Ludwig van Beethoven moved from Bonn to Vienna in 1792.
Ludwig van Beethoven studied composition with Joseph Haydn in Vienna.
Ludwig van Beethoven gained an early reputation in Vienna as a pianist and improviser.

key_moments.title: A letter kept private
key_moments.text: At **Heiligenstadt** outside Vienna, Beethoven wrote a letter intended for his brothers. In it he described his despair over his worsening hearing. He described suicidal thoughts and a renewed resolve to keep composing. The letter stayed among his papers and was discovered after his death.
claims: Ludwig van Beethoven wrote the Heiligenstadt Testament, a letter intended for his brothers, in 1802 while staying in Heiligenstadt outside Vienna.
Ludwig van Beethoven described his despair over his worsening hearing in the Heiligenstadt Testament.
The Heiligenstadt Testament describes Ludwig van Beethoven’s suicidal thoughts and his renewed resolve to keep composing.
The Heiligenstadt Testament was found among Ludwig van Beethoven's papers after his death.

key_moments.title: The Eroica at the Theater an der Wien
key_moments.text: Vienna's **Theater an der Wien** hosted a public performance of Beethoven's **Third Symphony**. The work was unusually long for a symphony of its time. Its second movement is a funeral march, and the symphony is known as the Eroica, or heroic symphony.
claims: Ludwig van Beethoven's Third Symphony was performed publicly at the Theater an der Wien in 1805.
Ludwig van Beethoven's Third Symphony was unusually long for a symphony of its time.
Ludwig van Beethoven's Third Symphony is known as the Eroica, meaning heroic.
The second movement of Ludwig van Beethoven's Third Symphony is a funeral march.

key_moments.title: Voices enter the Ninth
key_moments.text: An orchestra performed Beethoven's **Ninth Symphony** in Vienna. The first three movements were entirely instrumental. Then solo singers and a choir joined the orchestra for the finale, singing words from **Friedrich Schiller's** poem Ode to Joy.
claims: An orchestra performed Ludwig van Beethoven’s Ninth Symphony in Vienna in 1824.
The first three movements of Ludwig van Beethoven's Ninth Symphony are instrumental.
The finale of Ludwig van Beethoven's Ninth Symphony features vocal soloists and a choir singing words from Friedrich Schiller's Ode to Joy.

deep_facts.text: As Beethoven's hearing declined, visitors could talk to him by writing their remarks in notebooks. Some of these conversation books survive.
claims: Ludwig van Beethoven's visitors wrote their remarks in conversation books because of Ludwig van Beethoven's hearing loss.
Some of Ludwig van Beethoven's conversation books survive.

deep_facts.text: Beethoven wrote 33 piano variations on a single waltz by the publisher Anton Diabelli. The complete set is known as the **Diabelli Variations**.
claims: Anton Diabelli was a music publisher and composed the waltz on which Ludwig van Beethoven based his Diabelli Variations.
Ludwig van Beethoven's Diabelli Variations consist of 33 piano variations on Anton Diabelli's waltz.

connections.name: Joseph Haydn
connections.connection: Taught Beethoven composition after Beethoven moved to Vienna in 1792.

connections.name: Friedrich Schiller
connections.connection: Wrote Ode to Joy, whose words Beethoven used in the finale of his Ninth Symphony.

connections.name: Napoleon
connections.connection: Beethoven originally associated the Eroica symphony with Napoleon Bonaparte.

connections.name: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
connections.connection: Wrote Egmont, for which Beethoven composed incidental music.

connections.name: Congress of Vienna
connections.connection: Beethoven's cantata Der glorreiche Augenblick was performed during the congress.
